The truth

Simulator's terrain, fracture lines and hidden well types. The model never sees this.

What the model can see

Types read from the public-quality maps, with the simulator's own rule. Ringed wells are typed wrongly.

Zones: ground below its 1.5 km surroundings is valley, above is ridge; within 0.4 km of a fracture line is fractured rock. Low-yield wells (dark) are placed at random by the simulator, more often on ridges, so no map can show them; on the right they take the colour their location suggests. The model itself never assigns a type: it uses 13 terrain values from these maps as a starting guess for each well's behaviour.

Click a well on either map to see its details.

This is not Bengaluru

The city, its hills, fracture lines, lakes and wells are simulated: a stand-in of roughly Bengaluru's size, built to test the model against a known answer. The real 579 wells have no locations yet, so they cannot be placed on a real map. A real Bengaluru terrain map, from free satellite elevation data and without wells, is on the Bengaluru map page.

What the comparison shows

Public elevation maps get valley versus ridge right almost everywhere. Fractured versus weathered rock is where they fall short, because public fracture-line maps miss lines, misplace them and include lines that are not there. That is the layer worth improving first for real wells: a geology survey's fracture map, or a short pumping test.

More on terrain and maps →

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: vendor export (15 days, July 2026, in the vendor's real format but with demonstration water-level values), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (physics-based simulations of the 579 wells: one year in iteration 1, five years in later iterations and in Stage 2). No real water-level measurement has been used yet, and nothing here is yet a validated field forecast. Built by the FARII consortium.
